scope: Native physical placement/removal invariants compared to real GEMP Tremor/Disturbance deployments and production LoseInsertCardEffect. Native card-specific deployment, reveal effects and activation declaration integration are not claimed.
method: Six actual card deployments test minimum ordinary Reserve size, preserved ownership, unchanged Life Force and normal Reserve size, and thirty post-deployment shuffles per accepted case.
Two removal cases deliberately set the revealed flag, then execute production LoseInsertCardEffect; this tests destination and physical accounting, not reveal timing.

Native represents inserts as on-table records with private positions among ordinary Reserve IDs. GEMP keeps a combined internal list and filters inserts out of accounting. Equivalent observable invariants are compared, not internal representation or independent random orders.

Native conditional shuffle is uniform over permutations with an ordinary top card; exhaustive two-card tests verify all legal outcomes. Hidden counts/order, recovery/corruption and ordinary movement suspension have native tests.
limitations: This checkpoint supplies shared physical lifecycle and projection; no new card is admitted. Card-specific deployment/once-per-game rules, automatic reveal scheduling, reveal cancellation/response effects, normal/variable activation declarations and peek replacement integration remain required.
An exposed insert prevents ordinary Reserve removal until its provider resolves it. Providers must yield at this boundary; multi-card loops cannot silently skip the insert.
Reserve reshuffling with a revealed insert or no ordinary cards is guarded pending timing adjudication; no full-match coverage claim.
Whole native engine, broader catalog, ships/vehicles, Objectives/setup, formats, CPU/PvP, capacity and responsive full-match admission remain unfinished.
